model: The Dancing Demon — Plate Kinematics Model Framework
registration: R0.2 corrected global rotation; all positions evaluated in the common geographic frame

unknowns.units: Angular rate units are deliberately unspecified until a planetary time/scale convention is chosen
unknowns.reference_plate: Not selected; a reference may be fixed to zero only as a coordinate gauge, not as a physical claim

equations.rigid_plate_velocity: v_i(r) = omega_i × r, for unit position vector r on the sphere
equations.boundary_normal_component: v_n = v_ij · n_ij; n_ij points from face i toward face j. Positive is separation; negative is convergence.
equations.boundary_tangential_component: v_t = v_ij · t_ij; t_ij is the local boundary tangent. Nonzero v_t indicates transform-parallel motion.
equations.triple_junction_condition: For a triple junction at r, solve (u_TJ - v_i(r)) · n_ij = 0 for each of the three incident boundaries, with u_TJ constrained to the tangent plane.
equations.triple_junction_residual: The three boundary-normal constraints must admit one common tangent-plane junction velocity within a declared numerical tolerance.

required_tests: Sample each of the 21 boundary curves at multiple points, not only at its endpoints.
Determine the oriented boundary normal from the two adjacent face interiors; do not infer orientation from face names.
Resolve relative velocity into normal and tangential components along each boundary.
Detect sign changes in normal velocity along a boundary; if present, split the boundary into kinematic segments or classify it as mixed.
At all 14 triple junctions, solve the three normal-velocity constraints for one junction velocity and report residuals.
Check whether boundary classifications remain stable under increased sampling density.
Only after kinematics pass, combine motion with separately justified crust-type assignments.

classification_rules.divergent: Consistently positive v_n under the declared i-to-j normal convention.
classification_rules.convergent: Consistently negative v_n under the declared i-to-j normal convention.
classification_rules.transform: Normal component near zero while tangential component is materially nonzero.
classification_rules.oblique_or_mixed: Both components materially nonzero, or normal sign changes along the boundary.
classification_rules.unclassified: Velocity magnitude or component is below the declared resolution/tolerance.

crust_and_geology_separation: Plate face names do not determine crust type.
Convergent motion alone does not determine which side subducts.
Subduction requires an independently justified density/buoyancy and lithosphere-age model.
Continental collision, oceanic subduction, and oceanic spreading require different crustal context.
Mountain building and volcanism must follow from the resulting boundary process and crust type, not be assigned directly from the map.
acceptance_gates: All 21 boundaries have two identified adjacent faces and a stable orientation convention.
All 14 triple junctions pass the junction-velocity residual test.
Boundary classifications are stable under boundary sampling refinement.
Any assigned crust type is supported by a separate crust map and area accounting.
Any subduction polarity is supported by a density/age rationale.
No boundary type is assigned solely to make a desired mountain range or plot location possible.
limits: No angular velocity vectors or Euler poles have been selected.
No plate speeds, directions, crust types, subduction polarity, spreading centers, transform faults, or mountain belts are defined.
This file is a method specification, not a geodynamic model.
